_comment: The criterion-readability ratchet for PRODUCT_SPEC.md (SPEC INV-287, INV-288). Five arms, one per reading defect the 2026-07-27 and 2026-07-28 body surveys measured: a criterion that welds the whole rule into one sentence, a criterion that defines its own term in place while the glossary already owns that fact, a criterion whose closing clause has no finite verb, a criterion whose anchor competes with its prose, and a criterion whose pieces together carry more than one rule even when no single piece runs long. A criterion here is its numbered line together with the indented bullet lines of the sub-list under it, and each piece is one sentence for the measures: the long-criterion, inline-gloss, absolute-tail, and criterion-load arms read the criterion's body and every bullet, while the anchor-noise arm reads the criterion line for its three anchor readings and reports a bullet that carries a bracket code of its own. Each arm carries its own threshold and its own recorded baseline: the count of criteria that break it today. A count above the baseline reds. A count below it is a fall, and `--rebaseline` writes the lower numbers back; no run raises a baseline, and a raise is a deliberate edit here with its reason stated, run through the pipeline (INV-288).

long-criterion.reds: a criterion whose sentence runs past the word cap
long-criterion.fix: state the trigger and the duty and stop; move an enumeration into a sub-list, and a `since` or `so that` clause into its own short sentence or a note.

inline-gloss.reds: a criterion that defines a term in place, in a dash-pair aside or a parenthetical
inline-gloss.fix: give the term one glossary entry and let the criterion use it; a term not worth a glossary entry is not worth a gloss.

absolute-tail.reds: a criterion closing on a noun phrase with no finite verb
absolute-tail.fix: make the closing clause a finite sentence with its own subject and verb, or cut it.

anchor-noise.reds: a criterion whose anchor carries too many codes, or that runs a code anchor or code spans through its prose
anchor-noise.fix: an anchor needing four codes marks a criterion carrying four rules — split it; keep every code anchor at the line's end and cut the code spans the sentence can name in words.

criterion-load.reds: a criterion whose line and bullets together run past the total cap
criterion-load.fix: a criterion past this total carries more than one rule; split it into criteria of its own, a renumbering job that runs through the pipeline rather than a wording change.

reason: Baselines seeded at the row-148 readability landing, measured over the live PRODUCT_SPEC.md as the working tree stood on 2026-07-27 (1461 criteria): long-criterion 469, inline-gloss 120, absolute-tail 147, anchor-noise 61. The committed HEAD of that day measured 60 on anchor-noise over 1452 criteria, so the seed carries one unit from a delivery still in flight; the first run after the tree settles reports the fall and `--rebaseline` records it. Every later delivery lowers these or leaves them (INV-288). These four numbers were taken while the gate read the numbered criterion line alone. On 2026-07-27 the gate's reach widened to the criterion's bullet sub-list, so a run over a document that carries sub-lists measures more than the seed did. The numbers here stay as recorded until a run through the pipeline states the reason and writes the counts taken under the wider reach. The criterion-load baseline was seeded on 2026-07-28 over the live PRODUCT_SPEC.md as it then stood (1526 criteria): 42. It records a fact the other four arms miss, a criterion whose pieces sum past the total cap while no single piece runs past the per-piece cap, and it is seeded fresh rather than carried over from 2026-07-27 because that survey never summed a criterion's pieces. The criterion-load baseline was seeded at 42 on 2026-07-28 and lowered to 31 the same night: the sub-list repair had pushed eleven criteria past the total cap, each was trimmed back under it, and 31 is the count the document carried before that repair began. The other four arms keep their seeded numbers while sibling sessions are still editing the document, so a blanket rebaseline waits for a settled tree.
